business.text: Avenue Supermarts Limited (DMart) is a national supermarket chain focusing on value-retailing across multiple product categories. The group primarily operates on a cash and carry business model alongside sales to subsidiaries, making credit risk from receivables insignificant. The company operates brick-and-mortar stores alongside an online shopping service called DMart Ready.

cites.quote: Avenue Supermarts Limited (DMart) is a national supermarket chain, with a focus on value-retailing. We offer a wide range of products with a focus on the Foods, Non-Foods (FMCG) and General Merchandise & Apparel product categories.
The Company operates on business model of primarily cash and carry along with sales to subsidiaries and credit risk from receivable perspective is not significant.

narrative.text: The annual report highlights DMart's footprint expansion to 500 stores with 20.58 million square feet of retail business area as of March 31, 2026, operating on a low credit risk cash and carry model. On recent concalls, management agrees with this operational scale while placing greater emphasis on store ownership dynamics, noting that 68 out of 500 stores are leased and that DMart owns approximately 88% of its properties. Management also brings into focus operational headwinds not detailed in high-level financial summaries, such as warehousing rental inflation, wage pressures, deteriorated fixed asset turnover due to rising real estate costs, and managing the online DMart Ready service separately.

cites.quote: Since launching our first store in 2002 in Mumbai, Maharashtra, we have grown to 500 stores with a retail business area of 20.58 million sq. ft. spread across Maharashtra (128), Gujarat (75), Telangana (48), Andhra Pradesh (47), Karnataka (50), Madhya Pradesh (29), Tamil Nadu (35), Rajasthan (28), Punjab (24), NCR (20), Chhattisgarh (8), Uttar Pradesh (3), Uttarakhand (1), Goa (1), Orissa (1), Haryana (1) and Daman (1).
The Company operates on business model of primarily cash and carry along with sales to subsidiaries and credit risk from receivable perspective is not significant.
